results.title: Challenges and Trends in Experimental Psychology
results.content: # What are some current challenges and trends in experimental research in psychology? Experimental research is a powerful method to test causal hypotheses in psychology, but it also faces some challenges and trends in the current context. In this article, you will learn about some of the main issues and developments that affect experimental research in psychology, and how researchers cope with them. One of the challenges of experimental research in psychology is to ensure that it meets the ethical standards and principles of the discipline. Another challenge of experimental research in psychology is to address the replication crisis, which refers to the difficulty or failure of reproducing the results of previous studies. One of the trends of experimental research in psychology is to conduct online experiments, which offer some advantages over traditional laboratory experiments. Researchers have to use appropriate tools and platforms, such as online survey software, web-based experiments, or crowdsourcing platforms, to design and conduct online experiments. I think online experiment builders (e.g., Gorilla) are really improving access to experimental research methods, and will, hopefully, reduce the sole reliance on cross-sectional research (which until now has been much easier to complete due to the availability of online tools). Another trend of experimental research in psychology is to use mixed methods, which combine quantitative and qualitative data and analyses. A final trend of experimental research in psychology is to embrace open science, which refers to the movement and practices that aim to make the research more accessible, transparent, and reproducible. Open science can improve the quality and impact of the experimental research, by facilitating the sharing and reuse of the data, code, materials, and results, enhancing the collaboration and communication among researchers and stakeholders, and increasing the accountability and trustworthiness of the research. Open science also involves some challenges, such as dealing with ethical, legal, and practical issues related to the data protection, privacy, and ownership, and adopting the appropriate standards, formats, and platforms to disseminate the research. ### Experimental Research.
